source.citation: Written for Blackout, 2026-10-09, from the ABFM 2025 In-Training Examination critiques, items 164 to 175. Each question cites its item. Authoring batch for the ITE pool; review before trusting.

questions.q: A well 3-year-old with a soft continuous murmur below the clavicle, heard sitting, gone lying down. What is done?
d: Recheck the murmur in a month
questions.why: A venous hum is vibration in the neck veins, and its disappearance when supine is what makes it innocent. A patent ductus is also continuous but does not come and go with posture.

questions.q: Which features mark a murmur as a venous hum?
questions.why: The hum appears between 3 and 6 and needs no follow-up. A murmur that persists lying down or radiates is a different conversation.

questions.q: Anaphylaxis to tree nuts needed two doses of epinephrine; she now feels well. What is next?
d: Prednisone for five days and review
Famotidine daily and review in a week
questions.why: Needing a second dose makes the reaction refractory, and refractory or severe anaphylaxis carries a risk of a biphasic reaction hours later. Antihistamines and steroids are adjuncts afterwards, not the treatment.

questions.q: Why is severe anaphylaxis observed for hours after the symptoms have settled?
questions.a: A biphasic reaction can follow hours later
d: Epinephrine keeps working for twelve hours
Steroids take six hours to act
Allergy testing must be done the same day
questions.why: The second wave comes without a second exposure, which is why feeling well at the clinic door is not the end of the episode.

questions.q: Mechanical aortic valve, prior stroke and DVT, GFR 28, warfarin held for colonoscopy with biopsies. How is he bridged?
questions.why: His thromboembolic risk is as high as it gets and the procedure bleeds, so he needs full anticoagulation that can be switched off. Enoxaparin is out at that GFR, 5000 units is a prophylactic dose, and vitamin K is for the bleeding patient.

questions.q: What INR is targeted for a mechanical aortic valve in a patient with a prior embolic stroke?
questions.why: The higher range is for mechanical valves with added risk factors, which a prior embolic event is. Warfarin is resumed after the procedure with the same target.

questions.q: A 4-year-old with a buckle fracture of the distal radius. What is the management?
questions.a: A splint for 3 weeks; radiographs if pain persists
d: A splint for 3 weeks with routine radiographs
A cast for 6 weeks with routine radiographs
A cast for 6 weeks; radiographs if pain persists
questions.why: A buckle is an incomplete compression fracture with the cortex intact, so a splint, soft cast or wrap is enough. Choosing Wisely advises against follow-up films unless pain or tenderness persists.

questions.q: A 19-year-old home from college for a wellness visit. Which screening does the task force recommend?
questions.why: Drug use screening from 18 carries a B recommendation and covers nonprescribed use of psychoactive medicines or illegally obtained drugs. The other three are rated insufficient at this age.

questions.q: Which screens in adolescents and young adults does the task force rate as insufficient evidence?
questions.why: Insufficient means neither for nor against, which is not the same as recommended against. Anxiety, depression and drug use screening all carry B recommendations.

questions.q: Three days of large-volume milky-white watery stools in an oyster fisherman, non-toxic. Which pathogen?
questions.why: Rice-water or milky stool is the Vibrio signature, and it is tested for on that basis whether or not shellfish or brackish water are in the history. The other three are sought when there is fever, blood or mucus, sepsis or severe cramping.

questions.q: Which features of acute diarrhoea prompt stool testing for bacterial pathogens?
d: Three days of watery stool on its own
Shellfish in the past week on its own
questions.why: Rice-water stool is the one exception that is tested regardless. Most watery diarrhoea in a non-toxic patient needs fluids and nothing else.

questions.q: A 35-year-old with Down syndrome, no symptoms, labs two years ago normal. Which screening is due today?
questions.why: Hypothyroidism affects about half of adults with Down syndrome over 30, so the TSH is repeated every one to two years from 21. Dementia screening starts at 40, and bone density waits for 65 like everyone else.

questions.q: Which are recommended for adults with Down syndrome?
a: TSH every one to two years from 21
Dementia screening with a validated tool from 40
Cardiovascular prevention as for other adults
d: Dementia screening from the age of 30
questions.why: Atlantoaxial instability is commoner but no study supports screening films; the advice is to watch for myelopathy, meaning incontinence, gait change, brisk reflexes or clonus. Dementia before 40 is rare and gets a search for other causes.

questions.q: Day three at 9600 feet: breathless at rest, tachycardic, now coughing frothy sputum. What is done?
questions.why: High-altitude pulmonary oedema is an emergency and descent is the treatment. Acetazolamide prevents mountain sickness, dexamethasone is for cerebral oedema, and nifedipine is a stand-in when descent is impossible.

questions.q: When is nifedipine used to treat high-altitude pulmonary oedema?
questions.a: When descent or a hyperbaric chamber is unavailable
d: As the first treatment at any ski resort
For the headache of mountain sickness
questions.why: Its main role is prevention in people who have had HAPE before. The risk of mountain sickness climbs once people sleep above about 8200 feet.

questions.q: Which antibiotic is most often behind Stevens-Johnson syndrome?
questions.why: Sulfonamides account for most antibiotic-associated cases, and antibiotics as a class cause more than a quarter of all Stevens-Johnson and toxic epidermal necrolysis worldwide.

questions.q: One episode of postmenopausal spotting two months ago, endometrial stripe 4 mm, no polyps or fibroids. What follows?
questions.why: A stripe of 4 mm or less carries a negative predictive value above 99 percent for endometrial cancer. Biopsy would have been an equally good first test, but it is not needed after a reassuring scan.

questions.q: The spotting recurs despite a 4-mm endometrial stripe. What is next?
questions.why: Recurrent or persistent bleeding needs tissue whatever the scan showed. Hysteroscopy with curettage comes after a biopsy that fails to explain continuing bleeding.

questions.q: Shoulder pain with catching and popping after a fall on the outstretched arm, positive anterior slide test. Diagnosis?
questions.why: Catching or popping with a positive anterior slide test gives a likelihood ratio of 6 for a labral tear. A cuff tear brings weakness overhead and positive empty-can and external rotation tests instead.

questions.q: Which findings point to a rotator cuff tear rather than a labral tear?
questions.a: Weakness with a positive empty-can test
d: Catching and popping in the joint
questions.why: The cuff tear is a weakness problem and the labral tear a mechanical one. Pain on cross-body adduction with a tender joint is acromioclavicular arthritis.

questions.q: An adult screens positive for unhealthy alcohol use. What does the task force recommend next?
questions.why: Screening, brief intervention and referral to treatment reduces risky drinking, and the brief intervention is usually motivational interviewing. Referral is for patients who meet criteria for alcohol use disorder.
